title: Product and iterated derived internal bars, with augmentation normalization
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $G,H$ be profinite groups. Use the Grothendieck abelian categories $\mathcal A_1(A),\mathcal A_G(A),\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)$ of internal modules with condensed-group actions and the exact inflation adjunctions of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. Let $N$ be any $G\times H$-equivariant internal $A$-module, in degree zero. All derived functors are ordinary K-injective derived functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $A[P]$ for the free internal $A$-module on the condensed set represented by a profinite set $P$, and $R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A$ for internal module Hom derived in its second variable. For $a,b\ge0$ form the derived bicosimplicial bar with terms
$$B^{a,b}(N)=R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a\times H^b],N),$$
with the $G$- and $H$-inhomogeneous bar faces (first faces act on $N$) and degeneracies. Its totalization uses compatible nonnegative resolutions, with differential $d_G+(-1)^a d_H+(-1)^{a+b}d_{\rm res}$. Write $\operatorname{Tot}_\Delta$ for the totalization of its diagonal, whose degree $n$ term is identified with $R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[(G\times H)^n],N)$ by reordering coordinates.
There are natural derived identifications
$$\operatorname{Tot}_\Delta B(N)\cong R\Gamma_{G\times H}(N[0]),\qquad
\operatorname{Tot}_a\operatorname{Tot}_b B^{a,b}(N)\cong R\Gamma_G\bigl(R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])\bigr),$$
where the inner invariants retain the $G$-action. The diagonal-to-iterated comparison given by the augmented product group nerve and its two successive augmentations, with $H$ first and $G$ second, corresponds under these identifications to the right-derived comparison
$$R\Gamma_{G\times H}(N[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma_G R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])$$
induced by $N^{G\times H}=(N^H)^G$ and the specified inflation adjunctions. These are statements in the derived category of internal $A$-modules, including the comparison arrow. They are natural in $N$ and include either group trivial and $N=0$. No underived continuous-function complex is substituted for derived internal Hom.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation] the three action categories are Grothendieck abelian. Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $N\to I^\bullet$ in $\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)$, using [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] and successive embeddings of the cokernels. By [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] this is a K-injective representative of $N[0]$. The exact inflation to $G\times H$ has right adjoint $\Gamma_H^G$, so [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] makes every $(I^q)^H$ injective in $\mathcal A_G(A)$. Consequently $(I^\bullet)^H$ is also K-injective there, by the same bounded-below lemma. In particular it represents $R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])$, even though it need not resolve the degree-zero module $N^H$.

proof.text: Use [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] on the small profinite site: abelian sheafification is strong monoidal. Then [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] identifies internal $A$-modules with module sheaves over the same section-ring sheaf, preserving underlying sheaves and restrictions. The group actions are the same natural sectionwise families, so this also identifies the action categories. The balanced tensor and internal Hom agree under this equivalence: both balanced tensor products represent the same sectionwise bilinear maps, and their right adjoints agree by the adjunction bijections. We need ordinary injectives after forgetting actions. For a profinite $S$, $A[S]$ is the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{V\to S}A(V)$: maps from this presheaf to a module are precisely maps from the represented condensed set $S$ to its underlying sheaf. Thus it is $j_{S!}A_S$, flat by [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat]. Kernels of equivariant maps inherit their actions by restriction, and cokernels inherit actions on the sheafification of the sectionwise quotient. These constructions satisfy the kernel and cokernel universal properties equivariantly; a zero underlying sheaf has only one action. Hence forgetting actions detects exactness. The left adjoint of restriction $\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)\to\mathcal A_H(A)$ is $T\mapsto A[G]\otimes_A T$, with $G$ translating the first factor and $H$ acting on $T$. An equivariant map from it is uniquely $[g]\otimes t\mapsto g f(t)$. Flatness makes this adjoint exact. Likewise induction from ordinary modules to $P$-actions is $A[P]\otimes_A-$ for $P=G,G\times H$. By [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], restriction of $I^q$ to $H$, the underlying $I^q$, and the underlying $(I^q)^H$ are injective. The tensor and Hom used here are the closed module operations of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed].

source.place: Tags 03EV (lemma-j-shriek-flat) and 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor); explicit induction adjunction and equivariant kernel/cokernel argument

proof.text: Set $C^{a,b,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a\times H^b],UI^q)$, with $U$ forgetting both actions. The free universal properties identify $A[P\times Q]$ with $A[P]\otimes_AA[Q]$: maps out of either are the same $A$-bilinear families parametrized by $(p,q)$. The closed adjunction of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] then identifies $C^{a,b,q}$ with $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a],\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[H^b],UI^q))$. Step 2 and [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality] say that the $q$-complex in each bidegree computes exactly the derived internal Hom in the statement. All faces and degeneracies act on this single resolution. The two first faces commute since $(g,1)(1,h)=(1,h)(g,1)$; the other faces and degeneracies only change their own parameters. They also commute with the resolution differential because its maps are equivariant. Thus $C$ is a compatible bicosimplicial nonnegative resolution model of $B(N)$.

proof.text: Reordering $(G\times H)^n$ into $G^n\times H^n$ identifies the diagonal of $C$ with the single $G\times H$ bar on $I^\bullet$. The diagonal first face acts by $(g_1,h_1)$, because it applies the two commuting actions; an interior face multiplies both adjacent coordinates; the final face drops both final coordinates. The unit insertions agree as well. Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] to $G\times H$ and $N$: its resolution comparison identifies this diagonal total with $R\Gamma_{G\times H}(N[0])$, normalized by the invariant inclusion. Put $J^\bullet=(I^\bullet)^{G\times H}$. In this model that inclusion gives a quasi-isomorphism $j_D:J^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}_\Delta C$ supported in cosimplicial degree zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), formal product-to-successive augmented internal bar comparison; agent expansion

proof.text:
For fixed $a,q$ we verify the successive $H$ augmentation without assuming exactness of $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a],-)$. Write $P_{H,b}=A[H^{b+1}]$ with homogeneous $H$-action as in [lem-sfb-condensed-internal-bar-resolution]. Test the augmented $b$-complex on any profinite $S$. Its sections identify, by the closed adjunction, with the ordinary equivariant Hom complex
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_H(A)}(A[S]\otimes_AA[G^a]\otimes_AP_{H,\bullet},I^q|_H).$$
The tensor factor $T=A[S]\otimes_AA[G^a]$ has trivial $H$-action. The cited bar statement says $T\otimes_AP_{H,\bullet}\to T$ is exact, and step 2 says $I^q|_H$ is injective. Hom into an injective takes this augmented exact complex to an exact cochain complex: each restriction to an image subobject extends across the containing object, and the kernel is the Hom from the quotient. Thus the augmented section complex is exact for every $S$, and so is the sheaf complex. In homogeneous induced coordinates an equivariant map is determined at first coordinate $1$; its other values are $h_0$ times that value. Removing the first coordinate therefore gives the $H$ action face, interior removals multiply adjacent coordinates, and the last removes the last coordinate. Its degree-zero kernel is precisely $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a],(I^q)^H)$. The residual $G$ action respects the augmentation, since it commutes with $H$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), formal product-to-successive augmented internal bar comparison; agent expansion

proof.text: Put $K^{a,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a],(I^q)^H)$. The preceding augmentations give a map $k:\operatorname{Tot}_{a,q}K\to\operatorname{Tot}_{a,b,q}C$. To check it is a quasi-isomorphism, first fix $a$ and totalize in $(b,q)$: the augmented rows of step 5 are quasi-isomorphisms from $K^{a,q}$ in $b=0$. Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] with indices interchanged. The change between the two total conventions multiplies the $(b,q)$ summand by $(-1)^{bq}$, as substitution into $d_b+(-1)^bd_q$ verifies. Now apply the same comparison to the first-quadrant double complexes in $a$ and $b+q$. This proves the claim with the original triple differential $d_G+(-1)^ad_H+(-1)^{a+b}d_q$. Every degree involves only finitely many triples. No product exactness or unbounded convergence assertion is used.

Apply the homogeneous $G$ bar of [lem-sfb-condensed-internal-bar-resolution] to each $G$-injective $(I^q)^H$. For each profinite $S$ its augmented section complex is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_G(A)}(A[S]\otimes_AP_{G,\bullet},(I^q)^H)$ and is exact by injectivity, exactly as the image-and-quotient argument in step 5. The induced coordinates identify its unaugmented terms with $K^{a,q}$, including the first $G$-action face. The augmentation is $(I^q)^{G\times H}=((I^q)^H)^G$, with the literal equality of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. By [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison], transposing indices and multiplying by $(-1)^{aq}$ when changing total conventions, these rows give a quasi-isomorphism $j_K:J^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}_{a,q}K$. Since $(I^\bullet)^H$ is K-injective in $\mathcal A_G(A)$, its $G$ invariants compute $R\Gamma_G R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])$. Thus $k j_K$ identifies the triple total with this iterated derived object. This argument treats $(I^\bullet)^H$ as a complex, rather than incorrectly applying a module-only bar theorem to it.

source.place: Paragraph (3), formal product-to-successive augmented internal bar comparison; agent expansion

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bicosimplicial-shuffle-totalization] to $X^{a,b}=C^{a,b,\bullet}$ in the abelian category of internal $A$-modules. It gives the natural diagonal-to-iterated shuffle comparison $S:\operatorname{Tot}_\Delta C\to\operatorname{Tot}_{a,b,q}C$ in the derived category. The inclusion $J^\bullet\to C^{0,0,\bullet}=UI^\bullet$ is killed by both alternating first coface sums, because both groups fix it. The augmentation clause of that lemma therefore gives the equality of actual chain maps $S j_D=k j_K$. This is the augmented product-nerve comparison with $H$ first and $G$ second: its target differential has the ordered signs fixed in the statement, and its restriction along either successive augmentation is the given invariant inclusion. Since $j_D$ is invertible in the derived category, the equality also uniquely determines this comparison there.

source.place: Paragraph (3), formal product-to-successive augmented internal bar comparison; agent expansion

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] with $L_a:\mathcal A_1(A)\to\mathcal A_G(A)$ the trivial $G$-action inflation, $L_b:\mathcal A_G(A)\to\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)$ inflation along projection, and $L_c=L_bL_a$. Their right adjoints are respectively $\Gamma_G,\Gamma_H^G,\Gamma_{G\times H}$ by [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. That node also states that the conjugate of the inflation identification is exactly $M^{G\times H}=(M^H)^G$. Thus the normalized derived comparison is represented on $I^\bullet$ by the identity from $J^\bullet$ to $((I^\bullet)^H)^G$. By step 8 the bar comparison, after the identifications of steps 4 and 7, is represented by this same identity. The asserted equality of derived arrows follows; equality of cohomology maps alone has not been substituted for it.

source.place: Paragraph (3), formal product-to-successive augmented internal bar comparison; agent expansion

proof.text: For $N\to N'$ choose a lift between the nonnegative equivariant injective resolutions using [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists]. It gives maps of $C,K,J$ commuting with all augmentations and the shuffle. By [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality], these maps represent the stated derived maps. Two choices of lift are homotopic by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy]. Their postcomposition homotopies commute with the group operators. Multiply the homotopy on $C^{a,b,q}$ by $(-1)^{a+b}$ (on the diagonal by $(-1)^n$); the group-differential cross terms then cancel and the total homotopy equation is the original equation in resolution degree. The same argument applied to the identity of $N$ between two resolutions proves independence of the choice. This establishes naturality of the derived objects and of the comparison arrow.

source.place: Paragraph (3), formal product-to-successive augmented internal bar comparison; agent expansion

proof.text: If $G=1$ or $H=1$, all formulas still use the unnormalized constant group nerve in that direction; its positive alternating terms need not be zero. The bar augmentations of steps 5 and 7 and the shuffle lemma include a constant direction, so the same derived identifications and normalized comparison apply. If $N=0$, choose the zero resolution and every displayed complex and map is zero. Every parameter power is profinite in the fixed site and universe bound; all total diagonals are finite. At no point has internal Hom been replaced by sections of an underived continuous-function complex, nor has a free module on an arbitrary profinite set been assumed projective.
